conventions.convention: Simulation payoffs are jointly measurable and integrable at each parameter; oracle calls are individually integrable and unbiased, and their coupling is specified separately.
SPSA uses independent symmetric perturbation coordinates, nonzero almost surely, c > 0, and admissible perturbed parameters almost surely; invalid draws return zero before any oracle calls.
Scalar gradients are Euclidean column vectors, and vector expectations are coordinatewise.
The score identity uses a fixed sigma-finite dominating measure, common support outside one common null set, and an integrable density-derivative envelope on a neighborhood.
Conditional expectations and variances assume AC; vector conditional variance is the sum of scalar coordinate conditional variances.
The stochastic adjoint permits N = 0, defines its adjoint integrand as zero on the common measurable exceptional null set, and does not assume completeness of the probability space.

load_bearing.statement: For an admissible draw, call the oracle at θ + cΔ and θ − cΔ and return Ĝ_i = (Y⁺ − Y⁻)/(2cΔ_i); an invalid draw returns zero without oracle calls.
A simulation payoff is jointly measurable and integrable at each parameter; J(θ) = E[H(θ,·)]. A payoff-oracle call at θ returns an integrable real random variable Y(θ) with E[Y(θ)] = J(θ).

For the jointly measurable simulation payoff, a common almost-sure C¹ neighborhood, measurable gradient sections, a common integrable gradient envelope, and a square-integrable gradient at θ₀ imply Fréchet differentiability of J at θ₀, ∇J(θ₀) = E[∇θH(θ₀,·)], and finite coordinate variances.

Under AC, the stated C³ segment-neighborhood bound, independent symmetric nonzero perturbations with the stated reciprocal moments, conditionally unbiased calls, and weighted noise integrability, |E[Ĝ_i] − ∂_i f(θ)| ≤ M₃c²q_i/6 and the vector bias is at most M₃c²(Σ_i q_i²)^(1/2)/6.
Under AC and the deterministic weighted conditional second-moment bound B, E[‖Ĝ‖₂² | F] ≤ B/(2c²) and Var(Ĝ | F) ≤ B/(2c²).
For square-integrable outputs with any specified joint law and h > 0, Var((Y⁺ − Y⁻)/(2h)) = (Var(Y⁺) + Var(Y⁻) − 2Cov(Y⁺,Y⁻))/(4h²).

concerns.concern: The Definition inputs only 'a payoff oracle from [[def-simulation-gradient-objective-and-payoff-oracle]]' before evaluating it at θ ± cΔ. That supplier requires an integrable unbiased random variable at each fixed parameter, but no jointly measurable oracle realization or measurable probability kernel. These conditions do not ensure that the random-parameter calls, hence the returned estimator, are measurable. For example, take Θ = R, H = J = 0, θ = 0, c = 1, Δ uniform on [-2,-1] ∪ [1,2], and an independent centered Rademacher simulator input Z. For a non-Lebesgue-measurable A ⊂ [1,2], define the oracle family Y(η,Z) = 1_A(η)Z. Every fixed-η call is integrable and unbiased, and all algorithm input conditions hold. With shared Z, the returned output is (1_A(Δ) − 1_A(−Δ))Z/(2Δ), whose nonzero event is {Δ ∈ A ∪ (−A)}, which is not measurable. The algorithm therefore needs an explicit measurability condition on random-parameter oracle calls or on the oracle realization. The moment theorems separately assume conditional expectations of their outputs and are not refuted by this example.

Proof 1.1 says to apply the chain rule to 'u_{k+1}=Ψ_k(u_k,θ₀,ξ_{k+1})' while deriving Dθu_{k+1}=D_uΨ_k Dθu_k + DθΨ_k. The parameter must remain variable in the composition before evaluating its derivative at θ₀; freezing that argument literally removes the displayed direct parameter derivative. The intended composition is explicit in the Statement and the rest of the proof, so this is a local notation correction.

seams_checked.note: The central-difference supplier assumes C³ regularity on a neighborhood of the full segment and gives M₃h²/6. The SPSA bias proof applies it to g(t) = f(θ + tΔ), with third derivative bounded by M₃‖Δ‖³ on precisely such a neighborhood. The supplier page claims no stochastic or optimization conclusion.

The oracle definition supplies the vector conditional second-moment identity. The convergence proof meets Robbins–Siegmund with zero multiplicative error, predictable integrable decrement α_k‖∇f(x_k)‖², deterministic summable additive error, adapted integrable nonnegative X_k, and AC. Both page summaries preserve the distinction between moment assumptions and convergence conclusions; no minimizer or full-gradient convergence is inferred.

For N ≥ 1, freezing a valid sample produces the supplier's finite C¹ state-step graph with matching Jacobian dimensions and column-gradient convention. N = 0 is proved directly. Expectation interchange, measurability, and L¹ convergence of adjoint integrands are imposed separately by the consumer. Neither page infers derivative convergence from state or payoff convergence alone.
